clues.clue: DOT is the city agency in charge of these: streets, traffic signals, bike lanes, and the Staten Island Ferry.
clues.reveal: Transportation. The Department of Transportation (DOT) manages streets, signals, bike lanes, and the ferry.
clues.src_title: New York City Department of Transportation

clues.clue: DSNY, 'New York's Strongest,' is the city agency responsible for this daily pickup and snow removal.
clues.reveal: Sanitation. The Department of Sanitation (DSNY) collects trash and recycling and clears snow.
clues.src_title: New York City Department of Sanitation

clues.clue: HPD enforces the housing code and finances affordable units; the P and D stand for Preservation and this.
clues.reveal: Development. HPD, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development, enforces the housing code and funds affordable housing.
clues.src_title: New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development

clues.clue: The DOB reviews construction plans and issues the permits and certificates of occupancy for this.
clues.reveal: Buildings. The Department of Buildings (DOB) reviews plans, inspects construction, and issues permits.
clues.src_title: New York City Department of Buildings

clues.clue: City Planning, the DCP, writes the zoning rules and runs this seven-month public land use review, by its acronym.
clues.reveal: ULURP. The Uniform Land Use Review Procedure, run by the Department of City Planning, is the public process for major land use changes.
clues.app_title: Land use guide on the app

clues.clue: The LPC protects historic buildings and neighborhoods by designating them as these.
clues.reveal: Landmarks. The Landmarks Preservation Commission (LPC) designates individual landmarks and historic districts.
clues.src_title: New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission

clues.clue: NYC Parks maintains 1,700 of these green spaces, plus pools, beaches, and street trees.
clues.reveal: Parks. The Department of Parks and Recreation manages the city's parks, pools, beaches, and street trees.
clues.src_title: New York City Department of Parks and Recreation

clues.clue: DEP, the Department of Environmental Protection, delivers over a billion gallons a day of this from upstate reservoirs.
clues.reveal: Water. The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) runs the city's water supply, sewers, and water quality.
clues.src_title: New York City Department of Environmental Protection

clues.clue: The DOE is the nation's largest system of this kind, teaching about a million students.
clues.reveal: Public Schools. The Department of Education (DOE) runs the largest public school system in the United States.
clues.src_title: New York City Department of Education

clues.clue: Most city agencies are led by an appointed official with this title, chosen by the mayor.
clues.reveal: Commissioner. The mayor appoints commissioners to lead most city agencies; they serve at the mayor's pleasure.

clues.clue: Residents report potholes, noise, and missed pickups to any city agency through this 3-digit hotline and app.
clues.reveal: 311. The city's non-emergency hotline and app routes service complaints to the right agency.

clues.clue: At the most local level, 59 of these advisory bodies, like CB6 with its District Manager, weigh in on city services.
clues.reveal: Community Boards. The city's 59 community boards are the most local layer, advising agencies on land use, budget, and services.
clues.src_title: Community boards of New York City
